metadata.description: An explicit edge to openrouter:build-base, NOT `^build`. This entry point cannot compile before the parent's dist exists, so the edge is real -- but it has to be spelled out, because `^build` here would resolve to openrouter:build, which depends on this very target: a hard cycle. That XOR is the whole design constraint -- either the children get `^build` or the parent aggregates them, never both. Aggregating is the side that keeps one writer per dist directory. This is the widest child in the workspace: beyond the parent it also imports @dereekb/openrouter/firebase (a SIBLING entry point, hence a `build-base` edge -- siblings compile into this same dist directory and have no `build` of their own, so pointing at the parent's `build` here would close a cycle), plus @dereekb/analytics, @dereekb/date, @dereekb/rxjs, @dereekb/firebase-server/test and @dereekb/nestjs/openrouter. The last two are other families' CHILDREN, and by the cross-family rule they collapse to those families' ROOT `build` -- `firebase-server:build` and `nestjs:build` -- because a sibling family's child has no `build` of its own and writes into its parent's dist, so only the parent's `build` produces a finalized copy for TypeScript to resolve `exports` against. Neither closes a cycle: firebase-server and nestjs both sit upstream of openrouter and neither depends on it (nestjs-openrouter wraps the OpenRouter HTTP API directly, not @dereekb/openrouter).
